title: Echelon OSINT Source Registry
description: Machine-readable registry of OSINT data sources scored for settlement eligibility, mapped to the committed source_group_enum from OSINT_COMPOSED_ORACLE_V1. Derived from Gemini deep research (Feb 2026) with ChatGPT prioritisation and Opus corrections.

source_group_enum.description: Committed enumeration from OSINT_COMPOSED_ORACLE_V1_template.json. Sources MUST map to one of these values. Extension requires template version increment + fixture coverage.

sources.rate_limit_notes: 600 requests per 5 minutes. Stable for batch verification.
sources.notes: Official corporate filings and metadata. Stable company numbers as deterministic identifiers. Essential for entity verification in financial theatres. Identity verification changes under Economic Crime Act 2023 mean automated disambiguation heuristics still needed for officer matching.
sources.rate_limit_policy: 600 requests per 5 minutes. Stable for batch verification.

sources.rate_limit_notes: No published rate limit. RDFa/linked-data API with content negotiation (Accept: application/ld+json).
sources.notes: Winding-up petitions, creditors' voluntary liquidations, administrator appointments. Leading indicator (months before formal dissolution). Directly maps to counter_signal_checked failure mode in financial theatres: appearance of target entity in insolvency notice = automatic FAIL.
sources.rate_limit_policy: No published rate limit. RDFa/linked-data API with content negotiation (Accept: application/ld+json).

sources.rate_limit_notes: 10 requests per second. Requires User-Agent with contact email. Direct EDGAR preferred over third-party wrappers for ToS stability.
sources.notes: 13F holdings, insider trading (Forms 3/4/5/144), financial statements. Audit Reports API (via SEC-API, freemium) adds material weakness detection. For settlement-grade, prefer direct EDGAR over third-party APIs where possible. API endpoint: EDGAR full-text search. Direct XBRL: https://data.sec.gov/
sources.rate_limit_policy: 10 requests per second. Requires User-Agent with contact email. Direct EDGAR preferred over third-party wrappers for ToS stability.

sources.rate_limit_notes: No published rate limit. RESTful JSON with parameter filtering, sorting, pagination.
sources.notes: Federal debt, revenue, spending, interest rates. No auth required. Suitable for ledger reconciliation models pegged to federal rates or treasury yields.
sources.rate_limit_policy: No published rate limit. RESTful JSON with parameter filtering, sorting, pagination.

sources.rate_limit_notes: No published rate limit. JSON/XML/CSV output. SOFR, EFFR reference rates.
sources.notes: SOFR and EFFR rates are foundational for any escrow contract calculating interest accumulation. Pin series IDs in evidence bundles. Immutable baseline for rate-dependent settlement.
sources.rate_limit_policy: No published rate limit. JSON/XML/CSV output. SOFR, EFFR reference rates.

sources.rate_limit_notes: SDMX standard. Highly granular time-series via key parameter. Stable series identifiers.
sources.notes: Euro area price stability metrics, monetary policy decisions, historical exchange rates. SDMX format ensures stable schema. Good for macro-claims and FX-denominated waterfall settlements.
sources.rate_limit_policy: SDMX standard. Highly granular time-series via key parameter. Stable series identifiers.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Rate limited. Python/R client libraries available. Pin HS codes and reporter/partner pairs.
sources.notes: Official international trade statistics covering 99%+ of global merchandise trade. Good for commodity-linked claims, sanctions evasion detection, supply chain verification. Ensure cache and version pinning of query parameters.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Rate limited. Python/R client libraries available. Pin HS codes and reporter/partner pairs.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Self-hosted fork (AITOBIAS04/worldmonitor). AGPL-3.0 — consume via clean API boundary only, no code embedding.
sources.notes: 22-nation CII with 4-component weighted scoring, geographic convergence detection (3+ event types co-occurring), temporal baseline anomaly detection (Welford's algorithm, z-score thresholds). This is the primary evidence source modelled in OSINT_COMPOSED_ORACLE_V1 fixtures. Proto-first API with typed service contracts across 17 domains. Downgraded from settlement_grade: revision_policy is latest_only (composite scores recalculated), so source-level settlement requires witness_quorum or signed_receipt. Evidence bundles capture snapshots but the source cannot guarantee identical re-fetch.
sources.api_url_note: Self-hosted. API endpoint determined at deployment. Proto-first service contracts define the interface.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Self-hosted fork (AITOBIAS04/worldmonitor). AGPL-3.0 — consume via clean API boundary only, no code embedding.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Self-hosted fork. 92 stock exchanges, 19 financial centres, 13 central banks. 7-signal market radar.
sources.notes: Macro-level composite signals (BUY/CASH verdict, JPY/USD corridor, BTC hashing costs). Useful as corroboration for market-regime claims but composite nature means it is scoring-grade not settlement-grade. The underlying data sources (exchange feeds) may have licensing constraints at scale. Use for triage and macro-context, not entity-level settlement.
sources.api_url_note: Self-hosted. Finance Monitor variant. Endpoint set at deployment.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Self-hosted fork. 92 stock exchanges, 19 financial centres, 13 central banks. 7-signal market radar.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Self-hosted fork. AIS chokepoint monitoring. Defers full dark-fleet detection to paid providers (Spire/Kpler) in Phase 2.
sources.notes: Chokepoint vessel counts and AIS anomaly detection. Adequate for corroboration of strait-closure type markets. For settlement-grade maritime claims (insurance, shipping escrow), need Spire/Kpler with contractual SLA.
sources.api_url_note: Self-hosted. Maritime/AIS variant. Endpoint set at deployment.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Self-hosted fork. AIS chokepoint monitoring. Defers full dark-fleet detection to paid providers (Spire/Kpler) in Phase 2.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Free and open. Requires ~$500-800/month compute to produce oracle-grade structured events via BigQuery. 15-minute update cadence.
sources.notes: Global event monitoring, entity tagging, sentiment. The corroboration workhorse in OSINT_COMPOSED_ORACLE_V1 fixtures. Scoring-grade because GDELT's entity extraction has known precision issues — it correlates well in aggregate but individual event records can be noisy. Use for corroboration, never as sole primary evidence.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Free and open. Requires ~$500-800/month compute to produce oracle-grade structured events via BigQuery. 15-minute update cadence.

sources.rate_limit_notes: SDMX-based. Ensure series and version pins. Publication lag can be weeks/months.

sources.rate_limit_policy: SDMX-based. Ensure series and version pins. Publication lag can be weeks/months.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Community-maintained. Data can drift. Pin query + timestamp. Capture full response in evidence bundle.
sources.notes: Geospatial infrastructure verification. Powerful for shell-company detection (registered address vs actual zoning/infrastructure). Weak replayability because OSM edits are community-driven — same query may return different results next week. Always use as corroboration, never primary.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Community-maintained. Data can drift. Pin query + timestamp. Capture full response in evidence bundle.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Live bus arrivals (30s updates), TIMS traffic disruptions, tube crowding. Scope: London only.
sources.notes: Transport disruption as counter-signal. Sustained drop in network utilisation or traffic clustering around a logistics hub can signal operational bottleneck — counter to optimistic corporate press releases. Scope-limited to London but high-fidelity within coverage area.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Live bus arrivals (30s updates), TIMS traffic disruptions, tube crowding. Scope: London only.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Free but heavy pipeline. Pin product IDs + processing steps for determinism.
sources.notes: Physical asset verification (construction progress, mining activity, land use). Extremely high value but non-trivial integration. Defer to Cycle-038+. Deterministic if product IDs and processing chain are pinned.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Free but heavy pipeline. Pin product IDs + processing steps for determinism.

sources.rate_limit_notes: No published rate limit. Country code + date queries. Strong replayability — holidays don't change retroactively.
sources.notes: The precommitted HOLIDAY_CALENDAR discount rule in OSINT_COMPOSED_ORACLE_V1 fixtures depends on this source. Prevents false positives from routine activity drops on public holidays. Strong replayability. Essential counter-signal.
sources.rate_limit_policy: No published rate limit. Country code + date queries. Strong replayability — holidays don't change retroactively.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Free tier: 1 request/second, 100/day. Paid tiers available for volume.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Free tier: 1 request/second, 100/day. Paid tiers available for volume.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Alliance membership required for API. Grid telemetry, web traffic anomalies, smart-device indicators.
sources.notes: Power grid failure as counter-signal. If escrow awaits digital delivery from a datacentre and grid failure is detected, triggers grace-period protocol rather than breach. US coverage only.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Alliance membership required for API. Grid telemetry, web traffic anomalies, smart-device indicators.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Not a data source — a provenance primitive. Submits hash to calendar server, anchors Merkle root via Bitcoin transaction.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Not a data source — a provenance primitive. Submits hash to calendar server, anchors Merkle root via Bitcoin transaction.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Asynchronous query pattern. RESTful. Free API key required.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Asynchronous query pattern. RESTful. Free API key required.

sources.rate_limit_policy: 164M+ companies across 129+ registries. Free API with rate limits; paid tiers for volume.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Public CLOB. Market prices as implied probabilities. Subject to manipulation on thin markets.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Public CLOB. Market prices as implied probabilities. Subject to manipulation on thin markets.

sources.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API
sources.rate_limit_notes: Rate limited informally. Retrieve historical snapshots by domain + timestamp.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Rate limited informally. Retrieve historical snapshots by domain + timestamp.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Requires FCA authorisation (UK), PSD2 compliance (EU), or FDX registration (US). Explicit end-user consent per account. Ongoing regulatory obligations.
sources.notes: DEFER. Gemini correctly identifies this as the ultimate ground truth for LEDGER_RECONCILIATION and DISTRIBUTION_WATERFALL. But it's a 6+ month regulated integration, not an API key. FCA authorisation, consent flows, GDPR/PII obligations. Do not plan before Cycle-040+. When available, it would be settlement_grade primary_evidence.

For settlement-grade commodity pricing, use contractual exchange feeds (CME, LME) or official index providers.

sources.rate_limit_notes: JSON output. Retrieves corporation details and director information for federally incorporated entities. Does not cover provincially incorporated companies.

sources.rate_limit_policy: JSON output. Retrieves corporation details and director information for federally incorporated entities. Does not cover provincially incorporated companies.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Accessed via European e-Justice Portal. Connects national registers across EU member states. Confirms legal existence and basic status. Not as granular as individual national registries.
sources.notes: Partially fills the fragmented EU entity verification gap. Answers the binary question 'does this entity legally exist in any EU member state' through a single endpoint. Does not provide filing-level detail — for that, query the underlying national registry (INPI, Handelsregister, KVK). Scoring-grade corroboration, not settlement-grade primary evidence.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Accessed via European e-Justice Portal. Connects national registers across EU member states. Confirms legal existence and basic status. Not as granular as individual national registries.

sources.source_name: AFSA National Personal Insolvency Index API (Australia)
sources.rate_limit_notes: API channel for querying insolvency records. Strong replayability — insolvency records are immutable once published.
sources.notes: Closes Australian insolvency gap. Combined with ASIC (entity registry) and RBA rates (reference rate), makes Australia fully settlement-ready across all three legs. Counter-signal for financial theatres: appearance of counterparty in NPII triggers automatic risk escalation. Proposed judicial_record source_group pending v1.1.
sources.rate_limit_policy: API channel for querying insolvency records. Strong replayability — insolvency records are immutable once published.

sources.rate_limit_notes: 120 requests per minute. Thousands of economic time-series. Distinct from NY Fed Markets API — FRED covers broader macro indicators (GDP, CPI, unemployment, yield curves) not just reference rates.
sources.notes: Broader macro corroboration than NY Fed Markets. Series IDs are stable and deterministic. Good for economic-context claims in waterfall and reconciliation theatres. Scoring-grade because publication lag varies by series (some daily, some quarterly).
sources.rate_limit_policy: 120 requests per minute. Thousands of economic time-series. Distinct from NY Fed Markets API — FRED covers broader macro indicators (GDP, CPI, unemployment, yield curves) not just reference rates.

sources.rate_limit_policy: RESTful JSON output conforming to Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS). Covers public sector contracts above threshold values.

sources.rate_limit_policy: EU-wide procurement notices. Structured search and retrieval. Covers contracts above EU procurement thresholds.

Upgrade path to settlement_grade: register as ASIC DSP for direct SOAP access, change access_surface to partner_api, set settlement_eligible=true.

sources.source_name: Reserve Bank of Australia Statistical Tables
sources.rate_limit_notes: Published CSV/Excel downloads. No rate limit on file access. No official REST API exists.
sources.notes: RBA publishes statistical tables (interest rates, exchange rates, macro data) as downloadable Excel/CSV files. No official REST API. Third-party wrappers exist (readrba R package, community Lambda APIs) but none are authoritative. Cannot be settlement_grade due to portal_scrape access surface and day-level timestamp precision.

sources.rate_limit_policy: Published CSV/Excel downloads. No rate limit on file access. No official REST API exists.

sources.source_name: PACER — Public Access to Court Electronic Records
sources.rate_limit_notes: $0.10/page, capped $3.00/document. Fees waived if quarterly total ≤ $30. Large data pulls should run 6pm-6am CT per PACER guidance.
sources.notes: US federal court records. Two official REST APIs: Authentication API (username/password → token) and PACER Case Locator (PCL) API (REST, JSON/XML, nationwide case/party search). Official .gov source operated by the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts. Settlement-eligible: government system of record, REST API, token auth, deterministic case numbers.
sources.rate_limit_policy: $0.10/page, capped $3.00/document. Fees waived if quarterly total ≤ $30. Large data pulls should run 6pm-6am CT per PACER guidance.

sources.rate_limit_notes: Token auth. Rate limits apply. 501(c)(3) non-profit. Largest collection of PACER data outside the government.

The dedupe runner will correctly collapse these to one corroborator. Provides free fallback when PACER is unavailable, not independent corroboration.
sources.rate_limit_policy: Token auth. Rate limits apply. 501(c)(3) non-profit. Largest collection of PACER data outside the government.

proposed_source_group_guard.description: If proposed_source_group is present and template schema_version < 1.1, the runner MUST ignore it. In strict mode, fail schema validation.
proposed_source_group_guard.enforcement: Template runners MUST check schema_version before reading proposed_source_group. Sources with proposed_source_group are treated as their current source_group until the extension is committed.

revision_policy_settlement_guard.description: If revision_policy is 'latest_only', settlement_eligible MUST be false UNLESS receipt_mode_minimum is 'witness_quorum' or 'signed_receipt'. Mutable data cannot settle without compensating provenance.
revision_policy_settlement_guard.enforcement: Validator checks this invariant. Sources with latest_only + settlement_eligible=true + receipt_mode < witness_quorum will fail.

access_surface_independence.description: Two sources with the same independence_upstream_id MUST NOT both count toward corroboration_minimum_met. The verifier deduplicates by upstream_id before checking distinct source_groups.
access_surface_independence.enforcement: Theatre template runner must check independence_upstream_id uniqueness within each corroboration evaluation.

dubai_pulse_publication_layer.description: Dubai Pulse (api.dubaipulse.gov.ae) is a PUBLICATION LAYER, not a system of record. Multiple Dubai Pulse datasets may expose different views of the same backend system. The independence_upstream_id must reference the system of record (e.g., ae_dld_tabu for DLD data), not 'dubai_pulse'. Two Dubai Pulse datasets backed by the same system of record MUST NOT corroborate each other.

independence_upstream_dedupe_runner.description: Template runners MUST deduplicate sources by independence_upstream_id BEFORE evaluating corroboration_minimum_met. Two sources sharing the same upstream_id count as ONE corroborator regardless of having different source_ids or source_groups. This is a RUNNER requirement, not just a registry validation rule.
independence_upstream_dedupe_runner.implementation_note: At corroboration evaluation time: group evidence bundles by independence_upstream_id, collapse duplicates to single strongest-confidence entry, then count distinct source_groups from the collapsed set.
independence_upstream_dedupe_runner.enforcement: Runner-level. Registry validator checks for settlement-eligible upstream_id collisions as a warning. Full enforcement requires template runner integration.

http_transcript_canonical_spec.description: Canonical request representation for http_transcript receipt mode. All fetchers MUST normalise requests to this format before hashing to ensure deterministic receipt computation.

request_canonical.query_params: Sorted by key lexicographically. Values URL-encoded per RFC 3986. Duplicate keys sorted by value.

headers.sort: Sorted by key (case-insensitive), then by value

http_transcript_canonical_spec.hash_algorithm:
SHA-256 over: canonical_method + '
' + canonical_url + '
' + canonical_query + '
' + canonical_headers + '
' + body_hash
http_transcript_canonical_spec.note: This ensures two independent fetchers querying the same endpoint with the same parameters produce identical receipt hashes, regardless of HTTP library, header ordering, or default user-agent strings.

template_compatibility.note: Sources with proposed_source_group fields require template schema_version >= 1.1 before their proposed group can be committed. Registry runners on template < 1.1 MUST ignore proposed_source_group.
